easy.explanation: Rehoboam went to Shechem, where all Israel had come to make him king.
easy.q: Where did Rehoboam go to be made king?

easy.explanation: Jeroboam returned out of Egypt.
easy.q: Who returned out of Egypt?

easy.explanation: The verse says that all Israel came to Shechem to make Rehoboam king.
easy.q: Who came to Shechem to make Rehoboam king?

answers: Both occurred in preparation for Rehoboam’s kingship
Both came to speak with the elders
medium.explanation: Rehoboam came to be made king, and Jeroboam returned when he heard about it.
medium.q: What connection did Rehoboam’s arrival at Shechem have with Jeroboam’s return?

medium.explanation: The phrase means to establish Rehoboam as king.
medium.q: What does “to make him king” mean?

answers: He heard about the event and returned
medium.explanation: When Jeroboam heard what was happening, he returned out of Egypt.
medium.q: Why did Jeroboam return from Egypt?

answers: The event concerned the whole nation
The people had already rejected Rehoboam
challenge.explanation: The attendance of all Israel shows that the coronation was a national event.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from the fact that all Israel came to Shechem?

answers: He went from being in Egypt to returning to Israel
He went from being king to being a servant
He went from Jerusalem to Shechem
challenge.explanation: Jeroboam was first in Egypt and then returned from Egypt.
challenge.q: What change in Jeroboam’s situation is described in these verses?

answers: Jeroboam returned, then Rehoboam came to Shechem
Rehoboam came to Shechem, then Jeroboam returned from Egypt
All Israel departed, then Rehoboam arrived
challenge.explanation: Rehoboam’s arrival is described before Jeroboam’s return.
challenge.q: What is the correct order of events?

easy.explanation: Jeroboam and all Israel spoke to Rehoboam about the burden.
easy.q: Who asked Rehoboam to ease the burden?

answers: Ease the grievous servitude and heavy yoke
easy.explanation: They asked him to ease the labor and heavy yoke imposed by his father.
easy.q: What did the people ask Rehoboam to do?

easy.explanation: Rehoboam said, “Come again unto me after three days.”
easy.q: How long did Rehoboam ask to wait before answering?

answers: That they might serve Rehoboam more easily
That they might leave for Egypt
That they might add to the work
medium.explanation: They promised to serve Rehoboam if he eased the burdens placed upon them.
medium.q: What was the purpose of the people’s request?

medium.explanation: The yoke represents the heavy burden imposed upon the people.
medium.q: What is a “yoke” in this context?

answers: They left and did not return
They departed and came again on the third day
medium.explanation: The people departed and returned after the three days.
medium.q: What did the people do after Rehoboam asked for three days?

answers: They wanted to end all relationship with the king
They were willing to serve Rehoboam if he reduced the burden
They wanted to appoint another king immediately
challenge.explanation: Their promise connected relief from the burden with continued service to Rehoboam.
challenge.q: What does the promise “we will serve thee” reveal about the people?

answers: It set the time when the people would return for an answer
It caused Jeroboam to return from Egypt
challenge.explanation: The people returned on the third day to receive Rehoboam’s answer.
challenge.q: Why is the three-day delay important to the story?

answers: The heaviness of their labor and yoke
challenge.explanation: The people focused on the grievous servitude and heavy yoke.
challenge.q: What is the central subject of the people’s complaint?

easy.explanation: Rehoboam took counsel with the old men who had served before Solomon.
easy.q: With whom did Rehoboam first take counsel?

easy.explanation: They advised him to be kind, please the people, and speak good words.
easy.q: What did the elders advise Rehoboam to do?

answers: Those who had stood before Solomon while he lived
easy.explanation: They had stood before Solomon his father while Solomon was alive.
easy.q: Who were the old men Rehoboam consulted?

answers: The people would remain his servants
The people would leave the land
The people would make Jeroboam king
medium.explanation: The elders said the people would be Rehoboam’s servants for ever if he pleased them.
medium.q: What result did the elders expect from speaking kindly?

answers: The people would remain loyal and serve the king
The people would fight against the king
The people would move to Egypt
medium.explanation: The elders connected kind treatment with lasting loyalty.
medium.q: What does “they will be thy servants for ever” mean here?

answers: Leaving the land would produce service
medium.explanation: The elders believed that pleasing the people would cause them to serve Rehoboam.
medium.q: What cause-and-effect principle appears in the elders’ advice?

answers: The people requested relief, so the elders recommended a conciliatory response
The people requested war, so the elders recommended escape
The people requested another king, so the elders recommended greater burdens
challenge.explanation: Kind treatment directly addressed the people’s request for relief.
challenge.q: Why was the elders’ advice especially suitable to the situation?

answers: They had experience in royal administration
challenge.explanation: Their former service before Solomon presents them as experienced counselors.
challenge.q: What can be understood from the elders’ service before Solomon?

answers: The departure of all Israel from David’s house
challenge.explanation: According to the elders, kind treatment would have kept the people loyal.
challenge.q: What might have been preserved if Rehoboam had followed the elders’ counsel?

answers: The counsel of the old men
easy.explanation: Rehoboam forsook the counsel given by the old men.
easy.q: Whose counsel did Rehoboam forsake?

answers: The young men who had grown up with him
easy.explanation: He consulted the young men who had been brought up with him.
easy.q: With whom did Rehoboam take counsel afterward?

easy.explanation: They advised Rehoboam to add more to the people’s yoke.
easy.q: What did the young men advise concerning the yoke?

answers: The young men urged severity, while the elders urged kindness
The young men urged escape, while the elders urged war
medium.explanation: The elders advised kindness, but the young men advised increasing the burden.
medium.q: How did the young men’s advice differ from the elders’ advice?

answers: Rehoboam’s power or severity would exceed Solomon’s
Rehoboam was merely younger than Solomon
medium.explanation: The saying presented Rehoboam as stronger and harsher than his father.
medium.q: What did “My little finger shall be thicker than my father’s loins” communicate?

answers: He rejected the elders’ advice and sought another opinion
The elders sent him to them
medium.explanation: After forsaking the elders’ counsel, Rehoboam consulted the young men.
medium.q: Why did Rehoboam turn to the young men?

answers: That he would be more lenient than Solomon
That he would be stronger and harsher than Solomon
That he did not want to reign
challenge.explanation: Their advice emphasized that Rehoboam would add to Solomon’s burdens.
challenge.q: What image did the young men want Rehoboam to present?

answers: A favorable comparison between the two kings
challenge.explanation: The comparison portrays Rehoboam’s rule as more severe than Solomon’s.
challenge.q: What is suggested by the contrast between whips and scorpions?

answers: It could drive the people away from the king
It would send Jeroboam back to Egypt
It would cancel Rehoboam’s coronation at Shechem
challenge.explanation: The harsh policy led the people to reject the house of David.
challenge.q: What danger did the young men’s advice create?

paragraphs.paragraph: Rehoboam’s Answer and the Fulfillment of Prophecy
paragraphs.title: Rehoboam’s Answer and the Fulfillment of Prophecy

easy.explanation: They came on the third day, as the king had commanded.
easy.q: When did Jeroboam and the people return to Rehoboam?

easy.explanation: The king answered them roughly.
easy.q: How did Rehoboam answer the people?

easy.explanation: Rehoboam answered according to the advice of the young men.
easy.q: Whose advice did Rehoboam follow in his answer?

answers: The people accepted his rule without protest
The people asked Solomon to return
medium.explanation: The people did not hearken to the king and rejected the rule of David’s house.
medium.q: What was the result of Rehoboam’s harsh answer?

answers: A divine circumstance brought about the event
A place where the people lived
medium.explanation: The phrase identifies a divine purpose behind the outcome.
medium.q: What does “the cause was of God” mean in this passage?

answers: It was of God to fulfill the word spoken by Ahijah
There was a shortage of food
medium.explanation: The passage says the cause was of God, so that the LORD might perform his word.
medium.q: What deeper reason does the passage give for the king’s failure to hear the people?

answers: His harsh answer led to the outcome that fulfilled Ahijah’s word
He fulfilled the prophecy by easing the burden
challenge.explanation: The result of his harsh answer advanced the fulfillment of the word spoken by Ahijah.
challenge.q: How did Rehoboam’s words relate to the prophecy?

answers: The elders urged kindness, but Rehoboam answered harshly
The elders urged war, but Rehoboam answered kindly
challenge.explanation: Rehoboam rejected the elders’ recommendation to speak good words.
challenge.q: What is the main contrast between the elders’ counsel and Rehoboam’s answer?

answers: He adopted their policy of increasing the burden
He changed his mind and reduced the burden
He did not understand their counsel
challenge.explanation: He repeated the language about whips and scorpions and promised to add to the yoke.
challenge.q: What does Rehoboam’s repetition of the young men’s advice show?

paragraphs.idea: Rehoboam’s Answer and the Fulfillment of Prophecy

answers: They had a portion in David
They had no portion in David
easy.explanation: They asked, “What portion have we in David?” and declared that they had none.
easy.q: What did the children of Israel say after the king would not hearken?

easy.explanation: All Israel went to their tents.
easy.q: Where did all Israel go after speaking to Rehoboam?

answers: The Israelites dwelling in the cities of Judah
easy.explanation: Rehoboam reigned over the children of Israel who dwelt in Judah’s cities.
easy.q: Over whom did Rehoboam reign after Israel departed?

answers: Israel rejected the rule of David’s house
Israel wanted to strengthen David’s house
medium.explanation: The statement expressed separation from and rejection of the house of David.
medium.q: What did “see to thine own house” mean?

medium.explanation: Inheritance means a portion or possession, and the people denied having one in David.
medium.q: What is an “inheritance” in this context?

answers: It was limited to the Israelites living in Judah’s cities
medium.explanation: Only the people living in Judah’s cities remained under his rule.
medium.q: How did Rehoboam’s rule change after the people’s response?

answers: They returned separately to their homes and withdrew from the king
They agreed to the heavier burden
challenge.explanation: The expression describes the people’s departure from Rehoboam’s authority.
challenge.q: What does “every man to your tents” reveal about the people’s decision?

answers: All Israel departed, but those in Judah’s cities remained under Rehoboam
All Israel remained, while only Judah departed
challenge.explanation: The passage distinguishes between the departing nation and those who remained in Judah.
challenge.q: What contrast appears between verses 16 and 17?

answers: Rehoboam would not hearken to the people
challenge.explanation: The people separated after the king refused to listen to them.
challenge.q: What directly led to Israel’s separation?

paragraphs.paragraph: The Uprising and Revolt against David’s House
paragraphs.title: The Uprising and Revolt against David’s House

easy.explanation: Rehoboam sent Hadoram, who was over the tribute.
easy.q: Whom did Rehoboam send to the children of Israel?

answers: They stoned him with stones, and he died
easy.explanation: The Israelites stoned Hadoram, and he died.
easy.q: What did the children of Israel do to Hadoram?

easy.explanation: Rehoboam made speed to flee to Jerusalem.
easy.q: Where did Rehoboam flee?

medium.explanation: The verse identifies Hadoram as the man who was over the tribute.
medium.q: What was Hadoram’s position?

answers: Israel revolted against David’s royal dynasty
Israel returned to serve the king
medium.explanation: In this context, rebelled means revolted against the authority of David’s house.
medium.q: What does “Israel rebelled against the house of David” mean?

medium.explanation: After Hadoram was killed, Rehoboam fled to Jerusalem.
medium.q: What caused Rehoboam to flee to Jerusalem?

answers: It intensified the confrontation after the people had already rejected Rehoboam
It brought reconciliation between the people and the king
It caused the people to accept the tribute
challenge.explanation: The killing of Hadoram intensified the division between Israel and Rehoboam.
challenge.q: How did sending Hadoram affect the continuing conflict?

answers: The situation had become dangerous and forced him to escape
He went to make Jeroboam king
challenge.explanation: The uprising became dangerous enough that Rehoboam fled by chariot.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from Rehoboam’s flight?

answers: Rehoboam sent Hadoram, Hadoram was killed, Rehoboam fled, and Israel rebelled
Israel rebelled, Rehoboam sent Hadoram, and Hadoram became king
Rehoboam fled, then sent Hadoram, and the people accepted him
challenge.explanation: This is the sequence presented in verses 18 and 19.
challenge.q: What is the correct order of the final events?

paragraphs.idea: The Uprising and Revolt against David’s House
